title: Flip the agent-profile capacity warning to DEC-11's error in the release after the warning ships
description:
DEC-11 (opum-agent .quest/planning.json, accepted) rules: a profile whose declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget "ships first as a warning for one release, then as the error". LCLI-642 implements the warning half and makes this repository's four profiles fit so they do not warn; this task is the second half, filed at the time the first one landed so the ordering is held by a record rather than by memory.

The flip is deliberately a one-line change: a single exported severity constant in the check's core (LCLI-642 names it), so a reviewer reads exactly the change that turns every over-capacity profile from advisory to a failing gate. Nothing else about the finding moves -- same rule name, same message, same attribution, same profiles read.

Whose call this is: DEC-11's own scope clause says any lore check behaviour other than warning-then-error on capacity goes back to opum-doc. The flip is the approved second half, so it does NOT need a new decision -- but it does need the ordering VERIFIED, not assumed: the release that first ships the warning must be published before the flip lands, and that has to be read off released versions rather than inferred from intent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The flip is exactly the single severity line named by LCLI-642 -- no other production line changes -- and a reviewer pass records that

The flip lands in a release strictly after the release that first shipped the warning, verified against what was actually published (the tag/version carrying the warning exists and is older than the one carrying the error), not against intent or a plan
The release notes for the flip name it as a gate change, so a repository whose profiles are over capacity is turned red by a documented step rather than discovering it
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0, and lore-cli's own four profiles still do not warn before or after the flip
